narrative.overview: A Swiss watch movement seen from the back — the developer as watchmaker, a maker of precise working mechanisms. The world is committed dark: a graphite ground with brushed-metal raised surfaces, blued-steel screw detail, gilt engraving for labels and the primary action, and exactly one ruby jewel as the single bold colour. It refuses both the generic Swiss-Helvetica-grid it replaced and the dark-mode-neon-startup look — no glows, no saturated gradients, no candy accents. The register is calm, precise, and instrument-like: Schibsted Grotesk at 700 for the name and headlines, DM Mono for all machine data. Depth comes from tonal layering and hairline rules, not drop shadows. The one literal material is the hero's slowly-rotating brushed movement plate with its set ruby jewel.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite dark world, committed (color-scheme: dark), warm off-white ink.
One ruby accent, used only as a jewel — never as a fill.
Gilt for engraved labels and the primary button; blued steel for screw detail.
Two voices: Schibsted Grotesk (display/body) + DM Mono (all data/labels).
Depth by tonal plates + hairlines, not shadows.

rules.name: The One Jewel Rule
rules.body: Ruby appears only as a jewel — markers, links, focus rings, the set stone — never as a full-bleed fill or a wall. The closing CTA is a graphite plate with a gilt button, not a ruby band; if ruby ever covers a whole surface, the rule is broken.

rules.name: The Engraving Rule
rules.body: Gilt is reserved for two jobs: engraved mono labels and the single primary action. It is never body text and never a large fill.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Prose and headings are Schibsted Grotesk; anything that reads as machine data — labels, roles, tags, availability, buttons — is DM Mono, uppercase, tracked. A voice never crosses into the other's job.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by a 1px line border, never by a shadow. Depth is one tonal step (paper -> surface) plus a hairline. Reserve real shadows for literal three-dimensional metal (the movement plate) only.

dos: Do keep ruby as a jewel — small markers, links, focus rings, the set stone.
Do use gilt only for engraved mono labels and the one primary action.
Do separate surfaces with the line hairline and one tonal step, not shadow.
Do put all machine data (roles, tags, labels, availability, buttons) in DM Mono, uppercase, 0.08em tracked.
Do center content in a max-w-6xl column with px-6/px-10 gutters and py-20+ section rhythm.
Do keep motion opt-out: gate decorative animation behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and reveal-on-scroll behind html.js.
Do ship every visitor-facing string in both EN and FR (binding product constraint).
donts: Don't fill a surface with ruby or build a ruby 'wall' — the closing CTA is a graphite plate, not a ruby band.
Don't add drop shadows for elevation; reserve inset shadows for literal metal.
Don't introduce neon glows, saturated gradients, or a second accent colour.
Don't set body or heading text in gilt, or run prose in the mono voice.
Don't present the placeholder project images, portrait, or bios as real work.
Don't add a second display typeface or a system font — the pairing is fixed.
